data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describes it when the installation ritual is the only thing that distinguishes a 'mutation' from a 'guard'; the 1/9 loss in compile.py is a property of the ritual, not of the mutations, because every ordinarily-guarded module's 4/4 to 6/7 result is a description of the ritual's granularity, not of the code.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the number of guards per module is uncorrelated with the loss rate, the constraint is not from the ritual.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a different installation order produces the same 3-of-26, the test describes a stable property.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the mutations are pre-registered before installation, the ritual cannot constrain them.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The shown-to-fail-first installation makes the guard's failure a precondition for the mutation to exist as a test subject. The distribution of losses across modules is a description of how many guards each module has, not of how many mutations actually fail. The test constrains by construction because the subject is defined by the test's installation order.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
